title: Token-driven component showcase + dense table & chart guidance for docs site
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: The docs site currently documents tokens and components in isolation. Engineering and product teams repeatedly ask for concrete guidance on how tokens map to live component variants (buttons, tables, charts) and how to migrate from legacy token names. Goal: Ship a token-driven showcase page and a set of compact recipes that demonstrate density, contrast, and responsive token usage for buttons, dense tables, and charts. The showcase should be interactive (theme switcher + density toggle), include accessibility checks, and provide a clear migration table from legacy tokens to semantically named tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Docs site contains a 'Token Showcase' page that renders live component variants using current semantic tokens (color, spacing, radius, typography)
Buttons section demonstrates 6 states: primary/secondary/ghost disabled/active/focus with token overlays showing the token name for each visual property
Tables section includes 3 density presets (comfortable/compact/dense) with a toggle and code snippets showing the token-only changes required
Charts section documents color token sets (categorical/semantic/neutral) and includes contrast scores for each palette combination
Migration table lists legacy token -> new semantic token mappings with recommended fallbacks and codemod link
Accessibility notes accompany each example (contrast ratios, keyboard focus, row height minimums) and link to automated tests
Design + Engineering sign-off on docs copy and interactive playground (comment thread resolved)

migration_notes: Recommended flow: introduce semantic alias tokens in CSS variables, run codemod to replace legacy tokens across codebase, then delete legacy tokens in separate cleanup PR
Provide a minimal codemod snippet in examples folder: npx redwood-codemod replace-legacy-tokens --dry-run
If a customer uses custom token overrides, document how override values map to semantic tokens so migration is non-breaking
examples_to_add: Token preview grid with hover-to-copy token name and usage hints (eg. 'use for button background')
Button variants gallery showing tokens annotated on top of each CSS property (bg, border, radius, padding)
Table density toggle with CSS-only example and a React prop example: <Table density='compact' />
Chart palette selector that swaps token references and shows WCAG contrast score for selected foreground/background
Mini-playground component where teams can paste tokens.json and preview components with those tokens applied
do_dont_examples: DO: use semantic tokens (token-text-strong) instead of raw gray values — enables theme swaps and accessibility fixes
DON'T: hardcode pixel spacing into component markup; prefer token-space-* so density profiles can be swapped
DO: prefer named palettes for charts (token-palette-categorical-1) rather than ad-hoc hex arrays
DON'T: rely on token order for semantics; prefer explicit semantic keys so codemods can be safe
DO: include contrast checks in CI for any token change that affects text or critical UI elements

Tables: document new 'density' prop values and the exact token overrides applied for each density preset
Charts: add 'palette' prop docs that reference token names and link to recommended palettes for categorical vs semantic uses
All components: add a small 'tokens used' section that lists tokens for background, text, border, radius, spacing, and shadow
